gallery.filename: El Presidio de Santa Barbara, Canon Perdido Street and Santa Barbara Street, Santa Barbara, CA (53927828467).jpg
gallery.title: File:El Presidio de Santa Barbara, Canon Perdido Street and Santa Barbara Street, Santa Barbara, CA (53927828467).jpg
gallery.artist: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
gallery.description: Originally built in 1782, this complex of buildings were constructed by the Spanish Colonial Authorities of California to serve as a presidio to protect the nearby Mission Santa Barbara and serve as a center of political influence in the surrounding region.  The adobe buildings stood into the mid-19th Century, when they were slowly demolished and replaced by a neighborhood with roads platted through the middle of the presidio in the 1850s.  By the mid-20th Century, only a single structure, the El Cuartel, which is the second-oldest existing building in California, remained standing, having been transformed into a private residence.  The buildings were largely reconstructed after an archaeological investigation, with the first part of the complex being rebuilt between 1983 and 1985.  The buildings consist of one-story adobe structures with red terra cotta tile roofs, exposed rafter tails, porches with wooden columns, and small window openings surrounding a central dirt courtyard, which has been partially restored, and a larger and taller chapel at the center of the western end of the courtyard, with a gabled roof, an arched entrance bay, and small tower with two bells.  The buildings are divided by modern streets laid out after the Presidio had been largely demolished, with the ends of the reconstructed buildings revealing the interior structure of the presidio buildings where they are cut away along the streets.  The original buildings in the complex were listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.  Today, the reconstructed Presidio serves as a historical museum operated by the Santa Barbara Trust for Historic Preservation.
